author: Susana Carmona
description:
People say it looks like broccoli, a tree, a bowl, a pizza, a crescent moon, a Frisbee, a pancake. Etymologically, “pancake” is closest: Placenta means cake in Latin and comes from the Greek word plakoenta, which means flat cake. Per a Greco-Roman recipe that’s been dated to 160 B.C., in order to make the round, flat dessert called “placenta,” you need thin sheets of dough, cheese, honey, and bay leaves. If you’re trying to make the organ called “placenta,” the recipe is, of course, trickier than that.

Ancient civilizations gave the placenta great symbolic and spiritual importance. In some cultures, it was considered sacred because it protected the baby and represented the original mother-child bond. title: The Placenta Is More Powerful—and More Mysterious—Than You Think

author: Julie Moreno
description:
Most people know someone with Alzheimer’s disease. When I was growing up, my grandmother struggled with dementia, and I saw firsthand how difficult that was for our family.

That experience was one reason I became a neurotoxicologist who studies how misshapen proteins and inflammation in the brain can increase over time and cause dementia. While there are ways to treat the symptoms of dementia, researchers are still in search of a cure.
title: Why Old Dogs Might Be Able to Teach Alzheimer’s Researchers New Tricks
